accuracy.evidence: Each rule and reason matches standard child-safety guidance: RoSPA and Brake advise holding hands with young children near roads because under-fives cannot judge vehicle speed and drivers may not see them, and the Green Cross Code steps (stop, look, listen) are used in m8 and the road step. CAPT and the NHS warn that kettles, irons and pans stay hot enough to burn long after steam or flames stop, which is the basis of the teapot item, p3 and m4. Walking indoors to avoid trips and staying close in busy places to avoid getting lost are the topic's own evidence lines. No item suggests a child crosses alone.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the topic and in RoSPA/CAPT guidance: no visible steam or flame means safe (teapot prediction, challenge tag 'see', p3, m4), chasing a ball into the road (safe-choice prediction, first moment, m1), rules only count when a grown-up is watching (m3, adult text) and rules are just for fun or punishment (challenge tag 'why'). Running indoors 'to get there first' is tested by the walk step and m6, and wandering off in shops by the third moment and challenge tag 'alone'.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab has five scenes made only for this topic: a road where the cross button is refused until hands are held and two cars have passed, a hallway where running trips Kit on toys and walking reaches the door, a hot-or-OK kitchen sort, a rule-to-reason matcher that shows the rule's emoji on the matched reason, and three two-card safe-choice moments. gate_lab_distinct passes against every flagship, including flaghelp (help ladder) and flagplay.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child experiences each reason before the text names it: pressing Cross early gives 'Stop! A car is coming. Wait on the path', running makes Kit trip with a 'bump! ouch' pill while walking gets the 'safe at the door' pill, and putting the teapot in OK to touch gets 'it can be hot and burn you, even with no steam you can see'. The matcher then asks for the reason behind every rule, which is the topic's second evidence line (saying why each rule matters).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option shown false by the scene: 'Kit runs inside. What can happen?' ('Kit gets there fine', then Run trips Kit), 'The teapot has no steam now. Is it safe to touch?' ('Yes, no steam', then the teapot belongs in Hot) and 'Your ball rolls into the road. What do you do?' ('Run and get it fast', then the first moment rejects it with the reason). The done line repeats the child's choice and the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six questions with two tagged wrong options each, rotated every round. Each tag names the slip: 'fast' (rushing is how we get hurt), 'see' (you cannot always see hot; keep away from cookers, kettles and candles), 'alone' (on your own you could get lost), and 'why' (rules are not just for fun; each one stops us getting hurt). Wrong choices inside the lab also get scene-specific replies, such as the pan burning 'even with no fire you can see'.

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short lines with one rule and one reason each ('Inside, we walk. If we run, we can trip on toys and bump our heads.') and reads well under the family kid limit of 5.0; the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences to read at FK 7.3 against the 10.0 limit. The lab uses the young class, emoji on every card and button, and two-word pills (car coming!, road clear, bump! ouch).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content finds no filler and the explanation is under the 12% overlap limit with every lesson, including Asking for help and Playing alongside and together. Kid paragraphs are one rule each plus 'Every rule has a reason'; adult paragraphs cover age and progression, why reasons help, four named mistakes, and what each lab scene does. Practice and mastery items use different places (road, playroom, kitchen, shop, park).

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 (390 px) screenshots of every step before and after Show me: road, kerb lines and both pavements are distinct in dark theme after darkening the road, the hand-hold emoji and 'car coming!' pill stay on screen, the four rule and reason cards wrap their text inside the card at 11 px, the two safe-choice cards are large tap targets side by side, and the action buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a button: 'Hold hands', 'Cross the road', 'Walk to the door', 'Run to the door', 'The teapot is hot, stay away', each reason card, and each safe-choice option; dragging the child to the grown-up or a card to a box is optional. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the result and the next step (for example 'You hold hands. Now stop, look and listen. Wait for the cars.'). The walkthrough's axe WCAG 2.1 AA run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
